item.title: Local GP highlights availability of flu vaccines
item.description: It's not too late to get the flu vaccine - that's according to a Monaghan GP, who warns cases of flu are likely to rise over the coming weeks. The HSE predicted flu cases were expected to peak during Christmas week. Dr. Illona Duffy says while this week was not as bad as last week, we are not out of the woods yet. Advertisement

item.title: Gambling awareness highlighted locally
item.description: The first step in helping with a gambling addiction is accepting that there is a problem. That's according to Co Cavan gambling counsellor, Darragh King from Teach Oscail in Cavan Town. Darragh says recovery is a gradual process, but it is absolutely possible. Advertisement He says people do recover and you can live your life, but it can be daunting reaching out at the very start. item.title: Monaghan author reflects on former co-op
item.description: Monaghan Town Co-Op closed its doors one last time in 2025, after 124 years in operation. The local business had employed generations of local people during its over 100 years in existence. Joe Leonard from Smithboro launched his new book 'Heritage Destruction - The Death of a Co-op' on the business that was the fabric of the local economy for over a century. item.title: Woman dies after Fermanagh crash
item.description: A woman has died three weeks after a two-vehicle crash in county Fermanagh. Hanna Tanasova was involved in the collision between a car and a van on the Crom Road in Lisnaskea on December 5th. The PSNI said the 28-year-old, was originally from Ukraine but had lived in Mayobridge for several years. Advertisement She was taken to hospital along with a number of other people following the collision. Ms Tanasova died from her injuries on December 26th.

item.title: Castle Leslie Estate looks forward to 2026
item.description: The Executive Chef of Castle Leslie Estate says 2026 is looking even busier than 2025. Earlier this year, Snaffles Restaurant at Castle Leslie Estate won best hotel and guesthouse restaurant in Co Monaghan at the Ulster finals of the Irish Restaurant Awards. Castle Leslie also won 'rural destination of the year' at the Georgina Campbell Irish Food & Hospitality Awards, amongst other accolades over the past year.
